greeting: Good morning, Zuhair. A busy Sunday awaits, so grab a coffee and settle in.

lead.headline: Outside group finds AI is roughly doubling the pace of Anthropic's own research
lead.summary: The nonprofit METR reviewed 11 weeks of Anthropic's internal research data and concluded the company is developing its systems about twice as fast as a year ago, with AI tools a major driver. METR cautioned that Anthropic's redactions limit precision and that the speedup may apply mainly to well-specified tasks.

stories.headline: An AI-native lab that runs biomolecular experiments on its own
stories.summary: Published in Nature on 4 November, the paper describes an experimental laboratory built around AI that carries out varied biology experiments with minimal human intervention, going beyond earlier autonomous systems limited to single goals and simple instruments.

stories.headline: Making language models read raw bytes instead of tokens
stories.summary: A Nature paper (October 2026) shows how existing language models can be retrofitted to work over bytes rather than subword tokens, which matters for scientific data where tokenisation hides fine detail.

stories.headline: Scalable decision-making for games of imperfect information
stories.summary: Nature (October 2026) reports a method aimed at hidden-information games, tackling Stratego, a board wargame where established reinforcement learning and search approaches struggle.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber to approved security customers
stories.summary: The security-focused model is rolling out via the API and Codex to select customers, and OpenAI says it was trained to stay within authorised targets. It scored 48.5% on ExploitGym, up from 32.1% for its predecessor.

stories.headline: Thinking Machines reportedly in talks to raise $5-6 billion
stories.summary: Reports say Mira Murati's startup is negotiating a round at a valuation of at least $40 billion, with Accel leading and Nvidia possibly contributing about half. The deal has not been confirmed as closed.

stories.headline: AI is speeding up Anthropic's research, METR assessment says
stories.summary: METR's independent review found the acceleration is substantial but uncertain, and said Anthropic's own public risk report understates it.

stories.headline: Premier vows 'whatever changes' after delivery rider's fatal stabbing
stories.summary: Victorian Premier Ben Carroll promised action after delivery rider Jianming Feng was killed in the CBD, and a 51-year-old man has been arrested.

stories.headline: Vigil held for delivery driver killed in Melbourne CBD
stories.summary: Hundreds gathered to remember the rider, with many raising concerns about safety in the city.

stories.headline: Council wants 'glorified drive-through' Mernda town centre rejected
stories.summary: Whittlesea council opposes a revised car-centric plan beside Mernda station, with the decision to go to the planning minister after the November state election.

stories.headline: Melbourne and North Melbourne reach AFLW preliminary finals
stories.summary: Melbourne held off Geelong in a close qualifying final, while North Melbourne comfortably beat Carlton.

stories.headline: Paraguay's president resigns amid bank collapse and impeachment push
stories.summary: Santiago Peña stepped down on 5 November as the lower house moved toward impeachment over the Ueno Bank crisis.

stories.headline: Israel's president opens talks on forming a government after the election
stories.summary: Isaac Herzog accepted the certified results and began consultations, with Gadi Eisenkot emerging as the likely candidate to unseat Netanyahu.

thought: The best way to predict the future is to invent it. - Alan Kay
